The *Indriya Sutta* ("Faculties", Iti 62) is the thirteenth discourse in the third division (the *Tikanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka*, located at page 53 of the Pali Text Society edition [SuttaCentral]. In this short discourse, noble attainments are expounded in terms of three spiritual faculties (*indriya*) [SuttaCentral].

A full parallel to the discourse exists in the Chinese translation of the *Itivuttaka* at T 765.132 [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies passage-level parallels in the *Sekkha Sutta* (AN 3.85), the *Āsavakkhaya Sutta* (Iti 102), and T 765.132:10.0, alongside a resembling parallel in the *Sokhumma Sutta* (AN 4.16) and a citation in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 3) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive internal Pali reuse (106 matching passages across 17 texts), prominently aligning segments §2.1–2.4 of this sutta with the *Indriya Saṁyutta* (SN 48.31), the *Indriyakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.4), and the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records recurring framing formulas shared with numerous adjacent suttas of the *Itivuttaka* (such as Iti 61, 63, 64, 65, 66, and 67) as well as the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

No secondary literature passages in the dossier discuss this specific discourse directly; all retrieved references merely discuss the term *indriya* in the context of the five spiritual faculties, the *Indriya Saṁyutta*, or unrelated texts.
